blocks.text: Planning to Paint Your Home? Here’s What You Need to Know First

A fresh coat of paint can do wonders for your home. It’s not just about aesthetics, but about protecting your biggest investment, increasing property value, and showing pride in where you live. For Tacoma homeowners, where damp winters and sunny summers can take a toll on siding, residential exterior painting is more than just a cosmetic update, it’s essential home maintenance.

But before you schedule your professional painters and pick out the perfect color, it’s crucial to prepare your home properly. Think of it like getting your car ready for a long road trip, you wouldn’t just hit the gas without checking the tires, topping off fluids, and packing the essentials.

In this blog, we’ll guide you step by step through how preparing and planning to paint your home in Tacoma makes the process smoother, and explain how the team at Black Pearl Painters handles all the heavy lifting so you don’t have to stress. Whether you’re painting for resale or simply refreshing your space, good prep makes all the difference.
Why Prep Matters More Than You Think

When it comes to painting the exterior of a home, prep is everything. You could use the best paint in the world, but if the surface isn’t ready, if there’s dirt, mildew, peeling paint, or hidden damage, the paint simply won’t stick or last.
Proper preparation helps ensure:

items: Fewer touch-ups and problems down the road

blocks.text: Step-by-Step Guide: How Homeowners Should Prepare for Exterior Painting
1. Clear the Perimeter
Your painters will need space to work. That means clearing the areas around your home’s exterior walls:

items: Move patio furniture, planters, garden hoses, and toys
Trim back shrubs or tree limbs that touch the house
Mow the lawn and remove any debris

blocks.text: Bonus Tip: If you’re planning to do any landscaping or outdoor projects, wait until after the painting is complete.

blocks.alt: planning to paint, preparing your property for paint
blocks.title: Planning To Paint Your Tacoma Home For A Professional Exterior Paint Job?

blocks.text: 2. Secure Your Pets
Painters will be in and out, using tools, equipment, and maybe even ladders around your property. If you have pets:

items: Keep them indoors or in a separate fenced area
Let your painters know about any pets on-site
Make sure pet access to yards and exits is restricted for safety

blocks.text: 3. Communicate Special Needs
Got a vegetable garden near the siding? Need to keep a side gate closed for security? This is the time to talk with your painters about:

items: Sensitive areas or surfaces to avoid
Access to power outlets or water
Preferred working hours or noise concerns

blocks.text: At Black Pearl Painters, our project managers will do a full walkthrough with you before the job starts, so you don’t have to worry about remembering every detail.
4. Remove Wall Hangings & Outdoor Decor
If you’ve got decorative signs, string lights, security cameras, or mounted planters on your side, take them down. These should be stored away until painting is complete.
Also, temporarily remove window screens if your painters request it (some will do this for you as part of their prep process).

blocks.alt: planning to paint, preparing your property for paint
blocks.title: Planning To Paint Your Tacoma Home For A Professional Exterior Paint Job?

blocks.text: 5. Check for Repairs

If you’ve noticed cracked trim, soft wood, or peeling caulk, let your painters know in advance. Reputable exterior house painters in Tacoma (like us!) will inspect your home for needed repairs as part of the job quote.
At Black Pearl, we even offer carpentry repair services to handle minor fixes before we paint ensuring the best foundation possible.
6. Know What Your Painters Will Handle
You’re not on your own when it comes to prepping. In fact, at Black Pearl Painters, here’s what we take care of before the first coat goes on:

items: Power Washing: We remove dirt, mildew, and old flaking paint to give the new paint a clean surface to stick to.
Surface Repairs: Small holes, cracks, or damaged wood are addressed as part of the prep.
Caulking & Sealing: Gaps around windows, doors, or trim are sealed to keep moisture out and paint smooth.
Priming: We apply primer where needed, especially on bare wood or previously repaired areas.

blocks.text: What Happens If You Skip the Prep?
Shortcuts on prep lead to shortcuts in results. Here’s what you risk if you don’t properly prepare:

items: Bubbling or peeling paint within months
